name: IED, EA celebrates World Teachers Day in style

content.title: IED, EA celebrates World Teachers Day in style
content.summary: CELL holds workshop for educators on active learning

media.caption: Participants actively participating in a group discussion during the Development of Learner Competencies through Active Learning workshop held at the AKU campus in Dar es Salaam, Tanzania.
media.alt: IED, EA celebrates World Teachers Day in style

content.text: World Teachers' Day is a special occasion dedicated to appreciating and recognizing the hard work and dedication of educators worldwide. In celebration of this important day, the Centre for Continuing Education and Life Long Learning (CELL) through the Institute for Educational Development, East Africa (IED, EA) came together in a grand event to honor teachers by conducting a workshop on Developing Learner Competencies Through Active Learning. The workshop brought together over 65 pre-primary, primary and secondary school teachers, managers and heads of schools, daycare providers and other stakeholders in education.

The focus of the workshop was to enhance learners' understanding of active learning and how to facilitate it in their classrooms. With the paradigm shift in Competency- Based Curriculum (CBC) across East Africa, active learning is one of the key approaches that encourages students to engage with the subject matter actively. It shifts the traditional classroom paradigm from passive listening to active participation, fostering critical thinking, problem-solving skills, and a deeper understanding of the material. Research has consistently shown that active learning leads to improved academic outcomes and better retention of knowledge.

"This workshop is about active learning and how we can use active learning to build competencies. All those labels that are given to quality learning and teaching such as holistic education, student engagement, raising achievements etc. characterize active learning," said Dr Nicholas Wachira, Head of Programmes at IED, EA. "Therefore, this workshop is timely and useful because it serves to move us from not just focusing on the outcome of learning but to focus on the process. If you fix the process the outcome will come automatically."

Participants were first given color-coded sticker notes to share their opinions on what they believe to be the three characteristics of active learning. Following that, participants watched a video analysis on the use of active learning and learned how to incorporate effective active learning strategies into lesson plans. The session was quite interesting, and the way it was conducted itself was a good example of active learning.

Ms Linda Buramu, headteacher from Paragon Academy said, "Nothing is more boring than just sitting and listening in a class/workshop/training until the end without participation. To learn actively, we need to make sure that teaching enables active learning because active learning is more fun and exciting with lots of hands -on activities making the students to be fully engaged into learning with positive attitude and enthusiasm. Learners are able to share their thoughts, opinions and conclusions about a given topic which leads to high level of engagement, building self-confidence within the learners, increasing their motivation to learn as well as acquiring other skills such as innovation, critical thinking, reflection of real-life aspects, creativity, collaboration, communication, social-interaction and interpersonal skills."

IED, EA continues to honor the commitment to professionalizing the teaching profession by providing educators with the essential skills and knowledge required to thrive in today's evolving educational environment. This aligns seamlessly with this year's World Teachers' Day theme,
'The Teachers We Need for the Education We Want: The Global Imperative to Reverse the Teacher Shortage'
. It is crucial for teachers to embrace more engaging and effective teaching methods, which will ultimately yield benefits for students and society as a whole.

The workshop concluded with a reception, an excellent performance by kids from the Aga Khan Mzizima Secondary School and the Aga Khan Primary School Early Years Class, and the awarding of participation certificates.
